title: Short receipt that was a unit-of-measure error
brief: The Barcelona DC appears to have received far fewer coffee capsules (SKU C-777) than ordered on PO 8890. Find the root cause and an action plan.

evidence.content: PO 8890 ordered 10,000 units of C-777; the system recorded 1,000 units received on 6 Nov.
The supplier confirms the full 10,000 units were shipped.
The carrier delivered 1,000 cartons on 10 pallets with seals intact; the shipment weight matches 10,000 units at 10 units per carton.
On 30 Oct a master-data project changed the C-777 receiving unit from 'each' to 'carton', but the conversion factor was left at 1.
Correction: a physical recount of the PO 8890 receipt found 1,000 cartons x 10 = 10,000 units present.
C-777 demand is slightly below forecast.
Last month the same supplier short-shipped a different SKU (C-778) by 8%.

answer_key.root_cause: No physical shortage: a master-data change made 'carton' the receiving unit without a conversion factor, so 1,000 cartons (10,000 units) were recorded as 1,000 units.

remediation_rubric.criterion: Fix the conversion factor and correct the inventory record
Check other SKUs touched by the master-data project
Cancel any duplicate reorders or expedites triggered by the false shortage
Do not file a short-shipment claim with the supplier

answer_key.notes: E7 tempts a supplier-blame answer; E5 confirms the diagnosis late.

registry.mechanism_opportunities: V3: E3/E5 contradict E1; an alert can stop a supplier claim. D0 may chase the supplier (E7).
registry.expected_timing: Diagnosable in round 2 (E4); confirmed in round 3 (E5).
registry.favoritism_notes: Some V3 favour; balanced by HO-06.
